findings.finding: Genuit's H1 2026 interims (11 Aug 2026) report UK ventilation (Nuaire) sales and orders resilient, with ventilation orders up 6% on a last-twelve-months basis while revenue is flat, and ventilation markets stronger than RMI heating, a direct UK peer read that Volution's UK ventilation demand into FY27 is holding up despite weak construction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volution's outlook/current-trading lines: FY25 prelims ('new year has started well') +5.24%; FY24 prelims -4.58%; AGM trading updates +3.3% to +3.6% each of the last three years.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer document read through to a different company's new-year commentary; Volution's own UK business was flat in FY26 and its UK outlook has not been updated since 23 Jul. If the market had taken the read-through, FAN would have held the August highs rather than drifting from 692p to 654p with a flat 20-day run-up.
findings.independence: Proxy only; Volution's own pre-close (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/volution-group--fan/pre-close-trading-update/9682957) says UK refurbishment and social housing were 'resilient' and 'particularly strong', a different and earlier document pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The S&P Global UK construction PMI for August 2026 (published 4 Sep) shows residential at 37.6, the sharpest downturn of the sub-sectors and a 20th consecutive month of overall contraction (headline 44.3), so Volution's UK new-build channel is unlikely to have recovered in the first months of FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: UK weakness was flagged in the H1 results (12 Mar 2026, -1.6%) and the pre-close (23 Jul 2026, -0.63% close after +2.7% intraday); the stock has repeatedly faded good group numbers on UK caution.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro series are public, so this is mostly priced; what remains is whether Volution's first FY27 commentary on UK new build is more cautious than the July 'broadly flat' line. If fully priced, the July-to-October de-rating would have been accompanied by consensus cuts, and none was found.
findings.independence: The June PMI (38.4, housebuilding at its fastest fall of 2026) points the same way: https://www.lbc.co.uk/article/eb7973a9448d4040a7f2283d2f6634d4-5HjdcYF_2/ (2026-07-06).

findings.finding: Systemair's Q1 2026/27 report (May-Jul 2026, published 27 Aug) shows Nordic sales +10%, organic +8%, 'volume growth was favourable in all countries' and an outlook headed 'favourable', supporting Volution's Continental Europe (Nordic recovery) momentum into FY27.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Continental Europe was Volution's strongest region in FY26 (5.5-6% organic per pre-close); the Nordic recovery has been part of every statement since H1 and was not separately reacted to.
findings.why_not_priced: Cross-border peer read from a Swedish report that UK holders of a FTSE 250 name rarely carry into Volution's numbers; covers May-Jul, so it overlaps Volution's FY26 Q4 (already pre-released) and only partly the new year, which is why it is small.
findings.independence: Volution's own pre-close says 'a sustained recovery in the Nordics' (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/volution-group--fan/pre-close-trading-update/9682957), same direction, different and earlier document.

findings.finding: The getAir acquisition (EUR40m, LTM revenue EUR13.9m and adj. EBITDA c.EUR4.0m, 'immediately earnings accretive') adds inorganic FY27 growth that the release will quantify for the first time inside the FY27 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day itself moved the stock +9.0% (635p to 692p on 4 Aug 2026); fully given back since.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: public for two months and analysts will have added it. The residual is only how management frames it in the FY27 outlook. EBITDA of c.EUR4m against group adj. operating profit of roughly GBP100m+ is under 4%.

findings.finding: Genuit's H1 2026 interims describe cost inflation driven by the Middle East conflict, including rising virgin polymer costs, offset only by double-digit price increases from May, an input-cost headwind for Volution's injection-moulded and electronic products into FY27 margins.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volution has expanded organic margins through FY26 including after the March-April cost spike (pre-close 23 Jul 2026), so no margin miss has been tested on this name recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer-cost transmission is a hypothesis: Volution's own July statement reported margin expansion in all regions after the cost spike, which argues against it and is why the size is small. Shares the Genuit document with finding 1 but rests on a different fact (costs, not orders).
findings.independence: The August construction PMI coverage notes input prices and the Middle East conflict as pressures: https://www.pbctoday.co.uk/news/planning-construction-news/housing-causes-big-drop-august-2026-pmi/165380/
